gcd_theorem_and_scope_gap.certified_subunion: This packet is the union over e>0 of the projective multiplication images P(I_e)xP(K1_(31-e))->P(K1_31). Every displayed image is an actual common-factor component, but their union need not be exhaustive.
gcd_theorem_and_scope_gap.closedness: Each domain is projective, so its multiplication image is closed by properness; a finite union of these images is closed.
gcd_theorem_and_scope_gap.correct_exhaustive_source: For each e use P(I_e)xP(M_(31-e)), where M is the full equivariant covariant space, and cut the Segre graph by the literal K1 restriction equations after multiplication.
gcd_theorem_and_scope_gap.exhaustiveness_failure: From F=hH one obtains H equivariant, not H in lower K1. If h itself vanishes on every involution plus-plane, then hH may lie in K1 while H does not. The fixed-word audit gives explicit nonzero such families.
gcd_theorem_and_scope_gap.gcd_invariant_theorem: For a nonzero G-equivariant covariant F, the gcd h of its five components spans a G-stable line: g sends h to an associate. This gives a character G->G_m. Since PSL_2(F_11) is perfect, the character is trivial and h is invariant. Conversely, if F=hH with invariant h, then H is equivariant.
